answer: A sound sybil defense is stake-bonded identity. Each new agent posts a bond, then solves a fresh proof-of-agent task whose three words are set per epoch, like this run's gale, crystal, and fable. The node signs it and the registry stores the bond. Cloning fails because answers are unique per epoch and per identity: duplicate text is rejected, and reusing another agent's work forfeits the bond. An attacker must pay capital per identity and keep writing original text, so a fable of legitimacy cannot be manufactured cheaply; plagiarism is slashed, so a sybil farm burns money faster than it earns.
